results.title: Terms of the language of ordered rings
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Terms are built from variables $x_i$, one for each natural number $i$ (a de Bruijn index), and integer constants $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, using addition $s + t$, multiplication $s \cdot t$ and negation $-t$.

results.title: Formulas of the language of ordered rings
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: Formulas are built from the atomic formulas $s < t$ and $s = t$, for terms $s$ and $t$, and falsity $\bot$, by implication $\varphi \to \psi$ and universal quantification $\forall \varphi$, which binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$. Negation, truth, disjunction, conjunction and existential quantification are defined from these.

results.title: Negation of a formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negation $\neg\varphi$ of a formula $\varphi$ is the formula $\varphi \to \bot$.

results.title: The true formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The formula $\top$ is the negation $\neg\bot$ of falsity, that is, the formula $\bot \to \bot$.

results.title: Disjunction of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The disjunction $\varphi \lor \psi$ of formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ is the formula $\neg\varphi \to \psi$.

results.title: Conjunction of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the conjunction $\varphi \wedge \psi$ is the formula $\neg(\varphi \to \neg\psi)$.

results.title: Existential quantification of formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a formula $\varphi$, the formula $\exists \varphi$ is $\neg \forall \neg \varphi$; it binds de Bruijn index $0$ in $\varphi$.

results.title: Extending an environment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An environment is a map $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ that assigns a real number to each de Bruijn index. For $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the extension of $e$ by $x$ sends index $0$ to $x$ and index $i + 1$ to $e(i)$ for every $i \in \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Evaluation of terms
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given an environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of a term in $\mathbb{R}$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable with de Bruijn index $i$ has value $e(i)$, the integer constant $k$ has value $k$, and the value of a sum, product or negation of terms is the sum, product or negation in $\mathbb{R}$ of the values of its parts.

results.title: Satisfaction of formulas over the reals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an environment. Whether a formula holds under $e$ is defined by recursion on the formula: $s < t$ holds when the value of $s$ under $e$ is less than the value of $t$ under $e$; $s = t$ holds when these values are equal; $\bot$ never holds; $\varphi \to \psi$ holds when $\varphi$ holding under $e$ implies $\psi$ holding under $e$; and $\forall \varphi$ holds when, for every…

results.title: Quantifier-free formulas
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A formula is quantifier free if it contains no universal quantifier $\forall$.

results.title: Quantifier elimination over the reals
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Quantifier elimination is a map sending each formula $\varphi$ of the language of ordered rings to a formula $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$, subject to two requirements: $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free, and for every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a real number to each variable, $\operatorname{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ does.

results.title: Quantifier elimination yields quantifier-free formulas
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ is quantifier free.

results.title: Quantifier elimination preserves truth
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathrm{qe}$ be the quantifier elimination map on formulas. For every formula $\varphi$ and every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\mathrm{qe}(\varphi)$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$ if and only if $\varphi$ holds in $\mathbb{R}$ under $e$.

results.title: A real number is a square exactly when it is nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every environment $e : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$, the formula $\exists x.\ x \cdot x = a$ holds under $e$ if and only if the formula $\neg(a < 0)$ holds under $e$. In the first formula the bound variable $x$ is de Bruijn index $0$ and $a$ is index $1$; in the second $a$ is index $0$; in both, $a$ denotes $e(0)$. Thus $e(0)$ is a square in $\mathbb{R}$ exactly when $e(0) \ge 0$.

results.title: Sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integer $n$ is a sum of two prime powers if $n = p^a + q^b$ for some primes $p$ and $q$ and some natural numbers $a$ and $b$. Since the exponents may be $0$, the number $1 = p^0$ counts as a prime power here.

results.title: $2$ is a sum of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The integer $2$ is a sum of two prime powers, since $2 = 2^0 + 2^0$.

results.title: Integers below $2$ are not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $n$ is an integer with $n < 2$, then $n$ is not a sum of two prime powers, since every prime power $p^a$ is at least $1$.

results.title: Infinitely many Tribonacci numbers are not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(T_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, given by $T_0 = 0$, $T_1 = 0$, $T_2 = 1$ and $T_{n+3} = T_{n+2} + T_{n+1} + T_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $T_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.

results.title: Infinitely many Padovan numbers are not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(a_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the shifted Padovan sequence, given by $a_0 = 1$, $a_1 = 0$, $a_2 = 1$ and $a_{n+3} = a_{n+1} + a_n$, so that $a_{n+2} = P_n$ is the $n$-th Padovan number, where $P_0 = P_1 = P_2 = 1$ and $P_{n+3} = P_{n+1} + P_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $a_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.

results.title: Infinitely many Perrin numbers are not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(E_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Perrin sequence, given by $E_0 = 3$, $E_1 = 0$, $E_2 = 2$ and $E_{n+3} = E_{n+1} + E_n$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $E_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.

results.title: Infinitely many Leonardo numbers are not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(L_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the Leonardo numbers, the generalized Leonardo numbers $L_{1,n}$ with parameter $1$, given by $L_0 = L_1 = 1$ and $L_{n+2} = L_{n+1} + L_n + 1$. There are infinitely many natural numbers $k$ such that $L_k$ is not a sum of two prime powers.

results.title: Third-order recurrences with infinitely many terms not sums of two prime powers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are infinitely many sequences $(s_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of positive integers with all of the following properties: each value is taken by $s_n$ for only finitely many $n$; there are integers $c_0, c_1, c_2$ with $c_0 \ne 0$ and $s_{n+3} = c_0 s_n + c_1 s_{n+1} + c_2 s_{n+2}$ for all $n \ge 0$; there are no integers $d_0, d_1$ with $s_{n+2} = d_0 s_n + d_1 s_{n+1}$ for all $n \ge 0$; and $s_k$ is not a sum of two…

results.title: Variational characterization of projection onto a convex cone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Variational characterization of the projection onto a cone with complete carrier: `p` is the projection of `x` iff the residual pairs nonpositively with the cone and is orthogonal to `p`. The ambient space need not be complete.

results.title: Cone projection residual pairs nonpositively with the cone

results.title: Cone projection residual is orthogonal to the projection

results.summary: The residual of the cone projection is orthogonal to the projection.

results.title: Variational characterization determines the cone projection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A point satisfying the cone variational characterization is the projection.

results.title: Negative polar cone
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The negative polar is the standard dual cone of the negated set. Continuity makes its carrier closed without requiring completeness of the ambient space.

results.title: Membership in the negative polar cone
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Cone projection residual lies in the negative polar

results.title: Negative polar agrees with the inner dual of the negated cone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a complete ambient space, the negative polar agrees with Mathlib's inner dual of the negated carrier.

results.title: Moreau decomposition, polar form

results.summary: The cone projection's residual is the projection onto its negative polar. This accepts a Mathlib proper cone directly.

results.title: Moreau decomposition
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A point is the sum of its projections onto a proper cone and its negative polar, and the projections are orthogonal.

results.title: Bipolar theorem for closed convex cones

results.title: Consecutive sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ be natural numbers. The consecutive sums of $a$ form the finite set of natural numbers $a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ for indices $0 \le u \le v \le k - 1$.

results.title: Erdős Problem 356
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that there is a real number $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $a_0 < a_1 < \dots < a_{k-1}$ with $1 \le a_i \le n$ for every $i$, whose set of consecutive sums $a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ (for $u \le v$) has at least $c n^2$ elements.

results.title: Erdős Problem 356 has a positive answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a real number $c > 0$ such that for all sufficiently large $n \in \mathbb{N}$ there exist $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $a_0 < a_1 < \dots < a_{k-1}$ with $1 \le a_i \le n$ for every $i$, whose set of consecutive sums $a_u + a_{u+1} + \dots + a_v$ (for $u \le v$) has at least $c n^2$ elements.

results.title: Rank-one trilinear term
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: For a type $F$ with multiplication and types $A$, $B$, $C$, a rank-one trilinear term is a triple of functions $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$, $w : C \to F$ (its left, middle and right factors), representing one rank-one summand $u \otimes v \otimes w$ of a trilinear tensor decomposition.

results.title: Value of a rank-one trilinear term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a rank-one trilinear term over a semigroup $F$ with factors $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$, its value at $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$ is the product $u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$.

results.title: Trilinear rank at most $r$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. An array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ has trilinear rank at most $r$ when there are $s \le r$ and functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ for $i = 1, \dots, s$ such that $T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

results.title: Monotonicity of trilinear rank bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring and $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ an array. If $T$ has trilinear rank at most $r$ and $r \le s$, then $T$ has trilinear rank at most $s$.

results.title: Trivial upper bound on trilinear rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ finite types. Every array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ has trilinear rank at most $|A| \cdot |B| \cdot |C|$.

results.title: Trilinear rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types. The trilinear rank of a coefficient array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ is the least $r \in \mathbb{N}$ for which there are $s \le r$ functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with $T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

results.title: The trilinear rank is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types, let $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ be a coefficient array, and let $R(T)$ be its trilinear rank. Then there are $s \le R(T)$ functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with $T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$.

results.title: Decompositions bound the trilinear rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types, and let $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ be a coefficient array. If there are $s \le r$ functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ with $T(a, b, c) = \sum_{i=1}^{s} u_i(a)\,v_i(b)\,w_i(c)$ for all $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$, then the trilinear rank of $T$ is at most $r$.

results.title: Rank bounds via the trilinear rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a semiring and $A$, $B$, $C$ finite types. For every array $T : A \to B \to C \to F$ and every natural number $r$, $T$ has trilinear rank at most $r$ if and only if the trilinear rank of $T$ (the least length of a decomposition of $T$ into rank-one arrays) is at most $r$.

results.title: Trilinear tensors
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a field $F$ and types $A$, $B$, $C$, write $F^X$ for the $F$-vector space of functions $X \to F$. The space of trilinear tensors over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$ is the tensor product $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ over $F$.

results.title: Coefficient array of a trilinear tensor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ and $C$ be finite types, let $B$ be a type, and write $F^X$ for the space of functions $X \to F$. The coefficient map is the $F$-linear isomorphism from $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ to the space of arrays $A \to B \to C \to F$ that sends each pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ to the array $(a, b, c) \mapsto u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$.

results.title: Coefficients of a pure tensor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $A$ and $C$ be finite types and let $B$ be a type. For $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$, $w : C \to F$ and $a \in A$, $b \in B$, $c \in C$, the coefficient array of the pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ takes the value $u(a)\,v(b)\,w(c)$ at $(a, b, c)$.

results.title: The pure tensor of a rank-one term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. A rank-one trilinear term with factors $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$ determines the pure tensor $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ in the trilinear tensor space over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$.

results.title: Tensor rank at most $r$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$, $C$ types. An element $T$ of $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$ has tensor rank at most $r$ when there are $s \le r$ and functions $u_i : A \to F$, $v_i : B \to F$, $w_i : C \to F$ for $i = 1, \dots, s$ such that $T = \sum_{i=1}^{s} (u_i \otimes v_i) \otimes w_i$.

results.title: Tensor rank bounds agree with coefficient rank bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $A$, $B$, $C$ types with $A$ and $C$ finite, and let $T$ be an element of $(F^A \otimes_F F^B) \otimes_F F^C$. For every natural number $r$, $T$ has tensor rank at most $r$ if and only if its coefficient array $A \to B \to C \to F$, obtained by the canonical linear equivalence, has trilinear rank at most $r$.

results.title: Tensor rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types. The tensor rank of a trilinear tensor $T$ over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$ is the least $r \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $T$ is a sum of at most $r$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$.

results.title: The tensor rank is attained
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types, let $T$ be a trilinear tensor over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$, and let $R(T)$ be its tensor rank. Then $T$ is a sum of at most $R(T)$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$.

results.title: Decompositions bound the tensor rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $A$, $B$, $C$ be finite types, and let $T$ be a trilinear tensor over $F$ indexed by $A$, $B$, $C$. If $T$ is a sum of at most $r$ pure tensors $(u \otimes v) \otimes w$ with $u : A \to F$, $v : B \to F$ and $w : C \to F$, then the tensor rank of $T$ is at most $r$.

results.title: Matrix coordinates

results.title: Matrix multiplication tensor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and natural numbers $m$, $n$, $p$, the matrix multiplication tensor is the array over $F$ indexed by triples $((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ of an $m \times n$, an $n \times p$ and a $p \times m$ matrix coordinate, whose entry is $1$ if $j = j'$, $k = k'$ and $i' = i$, and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: Square matrix multiplication tensor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and a natural number $n$, the square matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is the matrix multiplication tensor for multiplying an $n \times n$ matrix by an $n \times n$ matrix. Its value at a triple of matrix coordinates $((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ is $1$ when $j = j'$, $k = k'$ and $i = i'$, and $0$ otherwise.

results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $m, n, p$ be natural numbers, and write $e_x$ for the standard basis vector with index $x$. The coordinates of the structure tensor $\sum_{i < m,\, j < n,\, k < p} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in $F^{m \times n} \otimes F^{n \times p} \otimes F^{p \times m}$ are the matrix multiplication coefficients: the coordinate at $((i, j), (j', k), (k', i'))$ is $1$ if $j = j'$,…

results.title: Square matrix multiplication rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and a natural number $n$, the square matrix multiplication rank of $F$ at $n$ is the tensor rank of the structure tensor of multiplying two $n \times n$ matrices over $F$: the least number of pure tensors whose sum is that structure tensor.

results.title: Square matrix multiplication rank equals the coefficient tensor rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and natural number $n$, the square matrix multiplication rank of $F$ at $n$ equals the trilinear rank of the square $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$.

results.title: Contracting the matrix multiplication tensor gives the matrix product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a field $F$, matrices $A \in F^{m \times n}$ and $B \in F^{n \times p}$, and indices $i < m$ and $k < p$, the contraction of the matrix multiplication tensor against $A$ and $B$ at output coordinate $(i, k)$ equals the entry $(AB)_{ik}$ of the matrix product.

results.title: Matrix multiplication rank exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real number $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over a field $F$ when $w \ge 0$ and there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication coefficient tensor over $F$ is a sum of at most $C n^w$ rank-one trilinear terms.

results.title: Rank exponents via the minimum tensor rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $w$ a real number. Then $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over $F$ if and only if $w \ge 0$ and there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the tensor rank of the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication structure tensor over $F$ is at most $C n^w$.

results.title: Monotonicity of matrix multiplication rank exponents
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $w \le w'$ be real numbers. If $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent for $F$, then so is $w'$.

results.title: Matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of a field $F$ is the infimum, taken in $[0, \infty]$, of the real numbers $w$ that are matrix multiplication rank exponents over $F$; it is $\infty$ when there is no such $w$.

results.title: Rank exponents bound the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a real number $w$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over a field $F$, then the matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of $F$ satisfies $\omega(F) \le w$.

results.title: Lower bounds for the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $W$ be an element of $[0, \infty]$. If $W \le w$ for every real number $w$ that is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over $F$, then $W$ is at most the matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$.

results.title: Direct rank bound for the matrix multiplication tensor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and natural numbers $m, n, p$, the coefficient tensor of multiplying an $m \times n$ matrix by an $n \times p$ matrix over $F$ is a sum of at most $mnp$ rank-one trilinear terms.

results.title: Direct decomposition of the structure tensor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $m, n, p$ be natural numbers, and write $e_x$ for the standard basis vector with index $x$. The matrix multiplication structure tensor $\sum_{i < m,\, j < n,\, k < p} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in $F^{m \times n} \otimes F^{n \times p} \otimes F^{p \times m}$ is a sum of at most $mnp$ pure tensors $u \otimes v \otimes w$.

results.title: Strassen's rank bound for $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is a sum of at most $7$ rank-one trilinear terms.

reading_title.source: Strassen's rank bound for $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication

results.title: Strassen's decomposition of the structure tensor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and write $e_x$ for the standard basis vector with index $x$. The $2 \times 2$ matrix multiplication structure tensor $\sum_{i, j, k < 2} e_{(i,j)} \otimes e_{(j,k)} \otimes e_{(k,i)}$ in $F^{2 \times 2} \otimes F^{2 \times 2} \otimes F^{2 \times 2}$ is a sum of at most $7$ pure tensors $u \otimes v \otimes w$.

results.title: Direct rank bound for the square matrix multiplication tensor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and natural number $n$, the square $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ is a sum of at most $n^3$ rank-one trilinear terms.

results.title: Exponent three for matrix multiplication rank
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the number $3$ is a matrix multiplication rank exponent over $F$.

results.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is at most three
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of $F$ satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3$.

results.title: The matrix multiplication exponent is finite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the matrix multiplication exponent of $F$, an element of $[0, \infty]$, is not $\infty$.

results.title: Exponents above the matrix multiplication exponent admit rank bounds
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\omega(F)$ be its matrix multiplication exponent and let $w > 0$ be real. If $\omega(F) < w$, then there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most $C n^w$.

results.title: Upper bounds on the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field, let $\omega(F)$ be its matrix multiplication exponent and let $w \ge 0$ be real. Then $\omega(F) \le w$ if and only if for every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$.

results.title: Rank bounds just above the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $\omega(F)$ be its matrix multiplication exponent, a finite real number. For every real $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the $n \times n$ matrix multiplication tensor over $F$ has rank at most $C n^{\omega(F) + \varepsilon}$.

results.title: Rectangular inner dimension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real aspect $k$, the rectangular inner dimension is $\lceil n^k \rceil$, the least natural number that is at least the real power $n^k$.

results.title: Rectangular inner dimension at aspect zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, including $n = 0$, the rectangular inner dimension at dimension $n$ and aspect $0$, namely $\lceil n^0 \rceil$, equals $1$, so aspect $0$ is the outer product of an $n \times 1$ matrix and a $1 \times n$ matrix.

results.title: Rectangular inner dimension at aspect one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the rectangular inner dimension at dimension $n$ and aspect $1$, namely $\lceil n^1 \rceil$, equals $n$, so aspect $1$ is square matrix multiplication without rounding.

results.title: Rectangular inner dimension at dimension one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every real aspect $k$, the rectangular inner dimension at dimension $1$ and aspect $k$, namely $\lceil 1^k \rceil$, equals $1$.

results.title: Rank exponents for rectangular matrix multiplication
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a field and let $k, w$ be real. Then $w$ is a rank exponent for rectangular matrix multiplication over $F$ at aspect $k$ when $k \ge 0$, $w \ge 0$, and for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are $C > 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$ the tensor of multiplying an $n \times \lceil n^k \rceil$ matrix by a $\lceil n^k \rceil \times n$ matrix over $F$ has rank at most $C n^{w + \varepsilon}$.

results.title: Rectangular matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$ and a real number $k$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(k)$ of $F$ is the infimum in $[0, \infty]$ of all real $w \ge 0$ with the following property: for every $\varepsilon > 0$ there are a real $C > 0$ and a natural number $N_0 \ge 1$ such that for every $n \ge N_0$, the coefficient tensor $\sum e_{ij} \otimes e_{jl} \otimes e_{li}$ of multiplying an…

results.title: Dual matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent of $F$ is the supremum, taken in the extended nonnegative reals $[0, \infty]$, of the set of real aspects $k \ge 0$ for which the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of $F$ at aspect $k$ equals $2$.

results.title: Dual exponent at most one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) \le 1$.

results.title: Coppersmith's rectangular exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model at aspect $0.172$ equals $2$: an $n \times \lceil n^{0.172} \rceil$ matrix times an $\lceil n^{0.172} \rceil \times n$ matrix costs $n^{2 + o(1)}$ arithmetic operations.

results.title: Coppersmith's 1997 bound on the dual exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) > 0.29462$.

results.title: Le Gall's 2012 bound on the dual exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) > 0.30298$.

results.title: Le Gall–Urrutia bound on the dual exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) \ge 0.31389$.

results.title: Williams–Xu–Xu–Zhou bound on the dual exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the dual matrix multiplication exponent $\alpha(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\alpha(F) > 0.321334$.

results.title: Naive bound for rectangular matrix multiplication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and every real $k \ge 0$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent of the arithmetic-circuit model at aspect $k$ is at most $2 + k$.

results.title: Circuit size and tensor rank give the same rectangular exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$ and every real $k \ge 0$, the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent at aspect $k$ defined by arithmetic-circuit size equals the one defined by tensor rank.

results.title: The rectangular exponent depends only on the characteristic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If two fields $F$ and $K$ have the same characteristic, then for every real $k \ge 0$ the rectangular matrix multiplication exponents of $F$ and $K$ in the arithmetic-circuit model at aspect $k$ are equal.

results.title: Conjecture that the square exponent is two
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that for every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model equals $2$.

results.title: Naive bound for square matrix multiplication
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3$.

results.title: Strassen's 1969 bound on the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le \log_2 7$.

results.title: Pan's 1978 bound on the square exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le \log_{70} 143640$.

results.title: Bini–Capovani–Romani–Lotti bound on the square exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3 \log_{12} 10$.

results.title: Pan's 1979 bound on the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le 3 \log_{436} 196$.

results.title: Pan's 1980 bound on the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le \log_{48} 47216$.

results.title: Schönhage's 1981 bound on the matrix multiplication exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every field $F$, the square matrix multiplication exponent $\omega(F)$ of the arithmetic-circuit model satisfies $\omega(F) \le \log_{110} 140600$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Parenthesization
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is a full binary tree whose leaves are labeled by indices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$: either a single leaf naming matrix $i$, or a product node with a left and a right parenthesization as factors. Labels may be repeated, omitted, or out of order.

results.title: Leaf indices of a parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The leaf indices of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices form the list of indices in $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ obtained by reading its leaves from left to right: $[i]$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the concatenation of the lists of the left and right factors for a product node.

results.title: Row count of a parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. The row count of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices with respect to $p$ is $p_i$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the row count of the left factor for a product node.

results.title: Column count of a parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. The column count of a parenthesization of $n$ matrices with respect to $p$ is $p_{i+1}$ for a single leaf naming matrix $i$, and the column count of the right factor for a product node.

results.title: Dimension-compatible parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is dimension-compatible with $p$ when, at every product node, the column count of the left factor equals the row count of the right factor, where row and column counts are taken with respect to $p$. A single leaf is always…

results.title: Valid parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns. A parenthesization of $n$ matrices is valid for $p$ when its leaf indices, read left to right, are exactly $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$, and it is dimension-compatible with $p$.

results.title: Scalar multiplication count of a parenthesization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $p = (p_0, \dots, p_n)$ be a vector of natural numbers, regarding matrix $i$ (for $0 \le i < n$) as having $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns, and let $r(T)$ and $c(T)$ be the row and column counts of a parenthesization $T$ with respect to $p$. The scalar multiplication count of a single leaf is $0$, and that of a product node with factors $L$ and $R$ is the sum of the counts of $L$ and $R$ plus $r(L)\,c(L)\,c(R)$.

results.title: Matrix-chain cost
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A matrix-chain cost is a pair of natural numbers counting the abstract events charged by matrix-chain ordering and reconstruction: the number of split candidates evaluated by the dynamic program, and the number of tree nodes emitted during reconstruction.

results.title: Total matrix-chain cost
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The total of a matrix-chain cost is its number of candidate evaluations plus its number of reconstruction nodes.

results.title: Matrix-chain result
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A matrix-chain result for $n$ matrices pairs a natural number, the reported optimal scalar multiplication count, with a parenthesization of $n$ matrices, the reported optimal parenthesization. The structure itself does not require the count to be minimal or to be attained by the parenthesization.

results.title: Matrix-chain ordering
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $n \ge 1$ and natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, where matrix $i$ of the chain ($0 \le i < n$) has $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$ columns, the algorithm computes, bottom-up by interval length, values $m_{i,j}$ for $0 \le i \le j < n$: $m_{i,i} = 0$ and, for $i < j$, $m_{i,j}$ is the least value of $m_{i,k} + m_{k+1,j} + p_i p_{k+1} p_{j+1}$ over $i \le k < j$, and the first split point $k$ attaining it is recorded.…

results.title: Matrix-chain ordering returns a valid parenthesization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the parenthesization returned by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is valid: its leaves are the matrices $0, 1, \dots, n - 1$ in order, each exactly once, and at every multiplication node the column count of the left factor equals the row count of the right factor, where matrix $i$ has $p_i$ rows and $p_{i+1}$…

results.title: Matrix-chain ordering reports the cost of its parenthesization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the scalar-multiplication cost of the parenthesization returned by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ equals the optimal cost it reports.

results.title: Reported matrix-chain cost is a lower bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$, all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$ and every parenthesization $T$ of $n$ matrices that is valid for these dimensions, the optimal cost reported by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is at most the scalar-multiplication cost of $T$.

results.title: Split candidates evaluated by matrix-chain ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ evaluates exactly $\binom{n+1}{3}$ split candidates.

results.title: Reconstruction size in matrix-chain ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ charges exactly $2n - 1$ reconstruction events.

results.title: Exact event count of matrix-chain ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the total number of events charged by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is $\binom{n+1}{3} + (2n - 1)$.

results.title: Cubic bound for matrix-chain ordering
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \ge 1$ and all natural numbers $p_0, \dots, p_n$, the total number of events charged by the matrix-chain ordering algorithm run on the dimensions $p_0, \dots, p_n$ is at most $3n^3$.

results.title: Multiple alignments
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: A multiple alignment with $k$ rows over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a finite list of columns, each of which assigns to every row $i \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ either a letter of $\alpha$ or a gap. No condition ties the rows to given sequences.

results.title: Valid multiple alignment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ rows is a valid multiple alignment of sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$ when no column of $A$ consists only of gaps and, for every $i < k$, deleting the gaps from row $i$ of $A$ gives $s_i$.

results.title: Induced pairwise alignment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is obtained by keeping, for each column $c$ of $A$ in order, the pair $(c_i, c_j)$, and dropping the columns in which both $c_i$ and $c_j$ are gaps.

results.title: Induced alignments have no all-gap column
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, no column of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is a gap in both rows.

results.title: Letters of the first row of an induced alignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, deleting the gaps from the first row of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ gives the same sequence as deleting the gaps from row $i$ of $A$.

results.title: Letters of the second row of an induced alignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, deleting the gaps from the second row of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ gives the same sequence as deleting the gaps from row $j$ of $A$.

results.title: Induced pairwise alignments are valid
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ be a valid multiple alignment of sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$. Then for all rows $i, j < k$, the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is a valid pairwise alignment of $s_i$ and $s_j$.

results.title: Pairs of rows
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the finite set of all pairs $(i, j)$ with $i, j \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ and $i < j$, so that each unordered pair of distinct rows appears exactly once.

results.title: Sum-of-pairs score of a column
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For a column $c$ of a multiple alignment of $k$ sequences, which gives each row $r < k$ either a letter or a gap $c_r$, the sum-of-pairs score of $c$ is $\sum_{i < j < k} s(c_i, c_j)$, where $s$ is the pairwise column score: $\sigma(a, b)$ for letters $a$ and $b$, $g$ for a letter against a gap, and $0$ for two gaps.

results.title: Sum-of-pairs score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Fix a score $\sigma(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}$ for each pair of letters $a, b$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$. For two entries $x, y$, each a letter or a gap, let $s(x, y) = \sigma(x, y)$ if both are letters, $s(x, y) = g$ if exactly one is a gap, and $s(x, y) = 0$ if both are gaps. The sum-of-pairs score of a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences is the sum, over the columns $c$ of $A$, of…

results.title: Score of an induced pairwise alignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, the score (with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$) of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ equals the sum, over all columns $c$ of $A$, of the column score of the pair $(c_i, c_j)$.

results.title: The SP score is the sum of the induced pairwise scores
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For every multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences, the sum-of-pairs score of $A$ equals the sum, over all pairs of rows $i < j < k$, of the score of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$.

results.title: Every family of sequences has a multiple alignment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every family of $k$ sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$ whose lengths sum to at most $n$, there is a valid multiple alignment of $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$.

results.title: Mean frequency across populations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean frequency `p̄ ω = (1 / n) ∑ X, p X ω` across the `n` populations.

results.title: Centred leaf covariance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The centred leaf covariance `K X Y = 𝔼[(p X - p̄) * (p Y - p̄)]`: the second moments of the frequencies centred across populations (not over `Ω`).

results.title: f2 from the centred leaf covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `f2` from the centred leaf covariance: `f2 X Y = K X X + K Y Y - 2 K X Y`.

results.title: Centred leaf covariance as the double centring of f2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The centred leaf covariance from `f2`: `K` is half the double centring of the `f2` matrix, `K X Y = (f̄2 X· + f̄2 ·Y - f2 X Y - f̄2 ··) / 2`.

results.title: f-statistics determine exactly the centred leaf covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: f-statistics determine exactly the centred leaf covariance. f-statistics see a model only through its centred leaf covariance: two square-integrable frequency models have the same `f2` at every pair (hence the same `f3` and `f4`, by `f3_eq_f2` and `f4_eq_f2`) if and only if they have the same centred leaf covariance.

results.title: Lineage weights of the three-population star tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Lineage weights of the star tree on three populations `0 = A`, `1 = B`, `2 = C`: edge `e` is the leaf edge of population `e`.

results.title: Lineage weights of the three-population admixture model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Lineage weights of the admixture model: `A` and `B` sit on edges `0` and `1`, and `C` is an `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` followed by drift on its private edge `2`.

results.title: Edge lengths of the star tree matching an admixture model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Edge lengths of the star tree matching the admixture model with edge lengths `a`, `b`, `c`: `(1 - α)(a + b)`, `α (a + b)` and `c - α (1 - α)(a + b)`.

results.title: Admixed population's weights in the admixture model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In the admixture model, `C` is the `α : 1 - α` mixture of `A` and `B` plus its private edge.

results.title: Star-tree model has binary loadings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The star-tree model has binary loadings.

results.title: Admixture model lacks binary loadings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `α ∉ {0, 1}` the admixture model does not have binary loadings.

results.title: Star tree and admixture model have equal f2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The star tree and the admixture model have the same `f2` at every pair of populations.

results.title: Star tree and admixture model have equal f4
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The star tree and the admixture model have the same `f4` (hence the same `f3`) at every quadruple of populations.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the matching star-tree edge lengths
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The matching star tree has nonnegative edge lengths when `0 ≤ α ≤ 1`, `a, b ≥ 0`, and the private drift of `C` is at least `α (1 - α)(a + b)`, i.e. when `f3 C A B ≥ 0` in the admixture model.
